texts.facts: Respondent No.2 passed the detention orders dated 03.06.2023 against the detenus under the provisions of Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land- Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act No.1 of 1986) (for short 'Act No.1 of 1986'), under the category of 'Dacoit' as defined under Section - 2 (c) of the Act No.1 of 1986. 4. In W.P. Nos.15973 and 16995 of 2023, the impugned detention orders were passed by respondent No.2 - detaining authority against the detenus - Mohd. Imran Khan @ Imran S/o Mohd. Aziz Khan and Md. Viquar Mehdi S/o Md.Khaja Pasha, respectively, relying on four (04) crimes viz., i) Crime No.27 of 2023 of Musheerabad Police Station, registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 395 and 419 of IPC and Section - 25 (1A) of the Arms Act, 1959, wherein the detenus robbed cash of Rs.40,000/- Mohd Sajid vs The State Of Telangana on 21 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138332866/ 1 KL,J & SKS,J W.P. No.15973 of 2023 & batch which was recovered and seized from their possession; ii) Crime No.14 of 2023 of Asifnagar Police Station registered for the offence punishable under Section - 395 of IPC, wherein an amount of Rs.35,000/- was recovered and seized from the possession of associate of the detenus representing part of extorted amount; iii) Crime No.32 of 2023 of Musheerabad Police Station was registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 395, 419 and 387 of IPC and Section - 25 (1A) of the Arms Act, 1959, wherein one knife, Suzuki Intruder Bike, mobile phone, Jio basic phone etc. were seized; and iv) Crime No.6 of 2023 of Santoshnagar Police Station was registered for the offence punishable under Section - 395 of IPC, wherein an amount of Rs.35,000/- was recovered from the possession of associate of the detenus representing part of extorted amount. In all the aforesaid crimes, the concerned Courts granted conditional bail to the detenus. On completion of investigation, the police laid charge sheets, and C.C. numbers are awaited. i) The allegations levelled in Crime No.27 of 2023 are that the detenus threatened the complainant at the point of knives with dire consequences to kill him and dragged the complainant into a lonely place in a lane beside Ramakrishna Medical Hall, where there was no KL,J & SKS,J W.P. No.15973 of 2023 & batch illumination and robbed cash of Rs.50,000/- and absconded on their bikes. While leaving the scene of offence, the detenus also threatened him to keep cash of Rs.3.50 lakhs ready by next day. ii) The allegations levelled in Crime No.14 of 2023 are that as per the directions of the detenus, their associate Muskan @ Heena called the complainant and took a selfie. Thereafter, the detenu in W.P. No.15973 of 2023 along with his associates called the complainant at King's Classic Function Hall, Gudi Malkapur, Hyderabad and showed the selfie photograph of the complainant with Muskan @ Heena and misrepresented that she is his wife and threatened the complainant with dire consequences and thereafter beat him and at the point of knives to kill him demanded an amount of Rs.4.00 lakhs. Out of fear, the complainant had paid an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- to the detenus. iii) The allegations levelled in Crime No.32 of 2023 are that the detenus along with their associates blackmailed the complainant showing false ID Card of Police Department and threatened the complainant with dire consequences while the other associates beat the complainant with hands and threatened him at the point of knives KL,J & SKS,J W.P. No.15973 of 2023 & batch to kill him and demanded an amount of Rs.10.00 lakhs, or else he would publish the news about the conversation with Syeda Uzma Fathima, an associate of the detenus. Out of fear, the complainant had agreed to pay some amount and asked the detenu in W.P. No.15973 of 2023 and his associates to come along with him to his house. The complainant paid an amount of Rs.2,70,000/- to the detenus and assured them that he would pay the remaining amount. iv) The allegations levelled in Crime No.6 of 2023 are that on 02.07.2022, Syeda Uzma Fathima (associate of the detenus) made a phone call to the mobile number of the complainant and discussed by misrepresenting the facts that she was intending to put an order of catering of food for 600 members. In pursuance of such misrepresentation, on 03.07.2022 under the guise of briefing and confirming the catering order, the complainant went to the terrace of Kings Khaja Hotel, Pisalbanda, Santoshnagar, Hyderabad, and while he was speaking to the said lady, the detenus Mohd Sajid vs The State Of Telangana on 21 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138332866/ 2 entered the room and beat and kicked the complainant alleging that he was misbehaving with the said lady. They threatened him with dire consequences and demanded an amount of Rs.10.00 lakhs to release him. Out of fear, KL,J & SKS,J W.P. No.15973 of 2023 & batch the complainant, the complainant had paid cash of Rs.5,000/- and an amount of Rs.40,000/- by way of online transfer . v) That apart, the detenu in W.P. No.16995 of 2023 had also past history of involvement in two (02) more crimes viz., i) Crime No.1026 of 2013 registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 384, 452 and 506 read with 34 of IPC of Panjagutta Police Station; and ii) Crime No.472 of 2016 registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 392 and 420 read with 109 of IPC and Section - 3 read with 4 of the Money Laundering Act, 2012 of Chikkadpally Police Station. 5. In W.P. No.16283 of 2023, the impugned detention order was passed by respondent No.2 - detaining authority against the detenu - Shaik Basheer S/ Shaik Chand, relying on two (02) crimes viz., i) Crime No.27 of 2023 of Musheerabad Police Station was registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 395 and 419 of IPC and Section - 25 (1A) of the Indian Arms Act, 1959; and ii) Crime No.14 of 2023 of Asifnagar Police Station was registered for the offence punishable under Section - 395 of IPC. i) The detenu had also past criminal history of involving in eight (08) more crimes viz., i) Crime No.6 of 2007 registered for the offence punishable under Section - 380 of IPC; ii) Crime No.145 of 2009 registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 323, 452 and 506 of IPC and Section - 25 (1B) of the Indian Arms Act, 1959; iii) Crime No.54 of 2010 registered for the offence punishable under Section - 324 read with 34 of IPC; iv) Crime No.79 of 2010 registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 452, 324, 323 and 506 read with 34 of IPC; v) Crime No.58 of 2011 registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 509, 506 and 323 of IPC; vi) Crime No.79 of 2016 registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 379 and 511 of IPC; vii) Crime No.88 of 2016 registered for the offence punishable under Section - 307 read with 34 of IPC and viii) Crime No.3 of 2022 registered for the offences punishable under Sections - 420 and 379 of IPC of Rein Bazar Police Station. 6. On completion of investigation, the police laid charge sheets and C.C. numbers are awaited. texts.arguments: Heard Mr. Pasham Trivikram Reddy, learned counsel representing Mrs. Ravula Sowmya Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioners, would submit that the impugned detention orders were issued without application of mind. The detaining authority did not consider the material properly. Therefore, there is no subjective satisfaction by the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention orders. Thus, the detention orders are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 8. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenus are serious and dangerous in nature and they formed into a criminal gang for committing such KL,J & SKS,J W.P. No.15973 of 2023 & batch grave and dangerous offences, such as dacoity/robbery/extortions by laying honey trap with their lady associates. The detaining authority, considering the entire material available on record and after arriving at the subjective satisfaction only passed the detention orders in order to prevent the detenus from committing similar offences. There is no error in it. i) He has also placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vijay Kumar v. Union of India 1 and Smt. K. Aruna Kumari v. Government of Andhra Pradesh 2. 9. Perusal of detention order, dated 03.06.2023, passed by respondent No.2 would reveal that the detenus along with their associates target the business/vulnerable people, beat them through a woman, trap them by taking photographs with such woman and blackmail them threatening the victims to make the photos public and also with dire consequences at the point of knives and extort money from them to earn easy and illegal money to lead a lavish life. It is also mentioned that the aforesaid crimes would amply demonstrate the habitual nature of committing crimes and creating large scale fear, terror and panic among the people adversely affecting the . Section - 2 (c) of the Act No.1 of Act, 1986 defines "dacoit" which means a person who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang commits or abets the commission of any of the offences punishable under sections 395 to 400 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration 3 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. . (1982) 2 SCC 403 KL,J & SKS,J W.P. No.15973 of 2023 & batch 14. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 4, the Apex Court held as under: "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State." 15. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar 5, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not characterize as an act of 'habitual'. The Apex Court was Mohd Sajid vs The State Of Telangana on 21 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138332866/ 5 of the opinion that to qualify as a 'habit', a person must have grown accustomed to leading a life of crime, whereby it would be a force of habit, inherent or latent, in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him as dangerous to society in general.
